sourceReviews.supportingSummary: JSON_MODIFY (Transact-SQL), Arguments/path and Example A, documents appending a string to an existing array while retaining prior elements. Arguments/newValue and the Remarks matrix distinguish ordinary string replacement, strict SQL NULL assignment, and lax SQL NULL deletion. All four proposed operations have supported outcomes; technical evidence does not establish adequate distractor quality.

choiceReviews.rationale: Contradicted: an ordinary update of the existing stages property replaces its value with the supplied nvarchar text. The derived document is {"stages":"verify"}, so neither original array element remains in that property. This exact option is valid for a different contract that replaces the collection with a single current-stage string. The existing-path/non-NULL matrix row supports that alternative, but it cannot satisfy array preservation.

Supported: append addresses the existing stages array and adds the new string after its current elements, deriving {"stages":["receive","validate","verify"]}. The path argument description and the documented append example establish this behavior. The literal input already supplies an array, so the question does not depend on creating a missing container. This is the correct operation for extending that exact sequence without substituting a scalar or null.

Contradicted: the stages path exists, and strict mode with SQL NULL sets its value to JSON null. The derived document is {"stages":null}, not an extended array. This unchanged expression is useful when the contract requires retaining the stages member while explicitly clearing its value. The source's NULL/existing-path matrix supports that countercontext; neither the retained member name nor strictness preserves the former array contents.

Contradicted: lax mode with SQL NULL deletes the existing stages member, giving {} for the shown one-property document. The same expression is correct for a removal request whose target is an empty object. It does not append a null element or retain the array under a null value. Those distinctions follow the documented lax deletion rule and the separate strict-null and append behaviors.
